prediction_question: For a chosen NOAA water-level station, will the daily maximum observed water level exceed its published minor flood threshold tomorrow?
prediction_time: End of the local day before the target day. Features are observed water levels only. NOAA tide predictions and model guidance are model output and must be excluded so the task stays an observation-only forecast.
target_definition: Binary: the daily maximum observed water level for the target day exceeds the station's NOS minor flood threshold from the CO-OPS metadata API, compared at datum=STND. The physical nos_minor threshold is retained by decision; it is not replaced with a per-station quantile merely to balance the classes (see measurements.target_threshold_decision).
datum_requirement: MUST use datum=STND. The published nos_minor threshold is in the station datum and the metadata API does not declare a datum. Comparing MLLW-referenced heights to nos_minor silently yields zero positives at every station; see measurements.datum_trap_measured.

review: Ready for construction on 2026-09-19. Contracts: redistribution read from the publishing portal (public domain, attribution requested, derived-not-official constraint recorded); prediction timing stated with an observations-only feature list; target derivable from the observed water level at datum=STND with the label source excludable; split capacity measured over the frozen 122-station list, eval 1,828 positives over 332 independent flood days and holdout 2,850 over 427. Extraction cost measured rather than estimated. The base rate at the physical threshold is 1.7-3.2%, which is a property of the phenomenon, not a defect: report precision/recall-style metrics beside AUC and use the base rate as the baseline. CORRECTION 2026-09-19: the 'product=daily_max does not exist' finding was wrong - the product is daily_max_min and it returns a station-year of 6-minute daily maxima per request, verified data with completeness flags. The primary task therefore costs 2,440 requests / ~178 MB, not 29,160 / 15.2 GiB.
next_action: Hugging Face is the missing destination: scripts/hf-publish.py still carries Austin's package path as a literal (PACKAGE = release/austin-911-response) and its repo id as a default, so publishing NOAA through it would describe Austin's dataset with NOAA's tag. Make it dataset-driven the way release-manifest.py was (read the release directory from the manifest or an explicit argument), then --plan/--create/--upload-small and the hf_publish worker job for the CSVs, then --verify. Then the pending consumer check against the transferred bytes (VERIFICATION.md names it), then operator approval before either destination leaves private. Separate open operator decision: whether to ship this task with the persistence floor documented (single feature 0.8265/0.8454 against model 0.8638/0.8688) or also build a harder variant.

prior_art: FloodCastBench, Sci Data 12:431 (2025) - inundation extent/depth, 30 m / 300 s, four events; not this task
NOAA ETSS/OFS operational guidance - forecasts, but publishes no scored ML task
novelty_check.theirs: NOAA publishes the observations, verified 6-minute daily maxima (daily_max_min, one request per station-year), the flood thresholds in station metadata, and annual flood-day counts (htf/annual). Operational forecasting exists (ETSS/OFS). FloodCastBench (Sci Data 12:431, 2025) covers hydrodynamic inundation dynamics for four events, not station-level exceedance classification.
novelty_check.ours: A leak-free next-day prediction task over a frozen 122-station panel: label = daily maximum water level at datum=STND exceeding the station's published NOS minor flood threshold, with observations-only features, temporal splits, and the label validated against NOAA's own annual counts (12/12 stations, 2025).
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.

task_design.target: does a station's daily maximum observed water level exceed its published NOS minor flood threshold on the next local day
task_design.prediction_time: the end of the previous local day; every feature is knowable then

label_source.product: htf/htf_daily.json, field minFlag (NOAA's own minor-flood days)
label_source.why: our reduction of 6-minute daily maxima overcounted flood days by ~20% against NOAA's own counts on a year with real signal (113-114 vs 94 over four stations, 2024); NOAA's flags matched exactly, station by station. Time zone was not the cause (GMT and LST differ by one day). A label that disagrees with the publisher's own product has to be justified, and there is no reason to ship one.

task_design.features: observations only, station-normalised: margin against the station's own published threshold, trailing mean/spread of its own maxima, days since its last exceedance, trailing-window exceedance counts, day-of-year. NOAA tide predictions and model guidance are excluded - they are not observations, and including them defeats the task. Station statistics use trailing windows only, so the future cannot leak into the features.

station_disjoint.rule: sort the 122 frozen stations by NOS station id; every third station is group0, the station holdout; train on group1+group2

task_design.why_this_is_the_contribution: NOAA publishes the observations, the verified maxima and the annual counts, so access is cheap and is not the contribution. A station-disjoint, leak-free, scored transfer task on a frozen panel is not published anywhere the novelty search found.

extraction_cost.breakdown: 2,440 for daily_max_min features (~178 MB) + 2,440 for the HTF daily flags (small), one request per station-year each

task_design.splits_cross_check: the three groups' positives sum to the temporal totals exactly (4307 + 3328 + 4251 = 11886), and the station group's station-days from the daily product equal the annual product's counts

feature_source.quality: verified maxima with pcComplete6Min and quality flags

construction_output.note: Complete panel: 122/122 stations and 2,440/2,440 station-years, 4,880 requests, zero fetch errors. The builder exits non-zero on any lost station-year, so coverage is a hard condition rather than a post-hoc observation.

qualification.result: PASSED - 32 checks per level, 0 failed, on both full artifacts, on the worker
qualification.note: Two earlier runs failed on coverage, not on the data: noaa-001 lost 13 stations and noaa-002 lost 60 station-years to fetch errors the retry treated as permanent. Both were fixed in the builder, which now records coverage and refuses an incomplete panel.

baseline.runner: the benchmark's own train.py and validate.py, copied verbatim; their sha256s are in the report, and validate.py re-ran training and reported CONTRACT OK on both levels
baseline.what_it_shows: the task is learnable, and the station-disjoint level scores the same as the temporal one (0.8688 against 0.8638) on stations the model never saw - so the signal is not station-specific memorisation
baseline.caveat: not yet calibrated against a persistence-only baseline. Yesterday's maximum against the station's own threshold is a strong feature, and consecutive flood days are common, so part of this AUC may be autocorrelation rather than prediction. A single-feature persistence baseline is the next measurement, before any headroom claim is made.

persistence_calibration.method: no training: rank-based AUC of each single stock feature, and of the plain rule 'yesterday's maximum exceeded the station threshold', on the eval split
persistence_calibration.verdict: the task is dominated by persistence: yesterday's maximum against the station's own threshold alone reaches 0.83-0.85 of the 0.86-0.87 the trained model achieves, so the model adds only 0.023-0.037. The task is real and it transfers across stations, but its headroom is narrow and a one-feature rule gets most of the way.
persistence_calibration.why_accuracy_is_not_used: the plain 'yesterday exceeded' rule agrees with the label about 96% of the time while carrying almost no ranking signal (AUC 0.63), because only ~2% of days are positive. Accuracy would flatter a useless rule; the runner contract scores AUC for this reason.
persistence_calibration.consequence_for_release: must be stated in the dataset card: the single-feature reference baseline belongs beside the model baseline, exactly as Austin records 0.627 for its single feature against 0.769 full model. A harder variant - onset after a dry spell, or a longer horizon, where persistence is weaker by construction - is the way to widen headroom if a low-headroom task is not wanted.
persistence_calibration.operator_decision: pending: whether to ship this task as-is with the floor documented, or also build a harder variant. The threshold itself is not being tuned.
